faq.q: Can I make beauty UGC ads from one product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear, straight-on photo and choose a routine, swatch, unboxing, or review scene. The result keeps the product as the subject, so compare the shade and package before posting.

faq.q: Will the video match my exact foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color comes from your photo and your wording, so shoot in daylight and name the shade plainly, like "warm beige liquid" or "brick red matte." If the tone drifts, make another version; the credit cost is shown before each one.

faq.q: Can I add my price or a promo code to the image?
faq.a: Type prices, promo codes, and product names afterward in Canva or CapCut. Lettering made by AI can be misspelled, so keep the image clean and add the words yourself.

faq.q: What kind of product photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: Use a straight-on shot with the label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands or clutter. Glossy tubes and clear glass pick up glare, so shoot beside a window rather than using flash.

faq.q: How long should a beauty ad video be?
faq.a: Pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds for feed ads. Use a shorter length for one action such as a swatch or pump, and 30 seconds for a longer routine; the credit cost is shown before each length.

faq.q: Can I use the same product photo for a white background shot and a routine video?
faq.a: Yes. Shoot the bottle, tube, or jar straight-on with the whole label visible, and use that file for both the white background photo and a routine or demo video. Keep the original uncropped so the vertical video can reframe without cutting the cap.

faq.q: Can I run the videos as paid beauty ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid social ads. Keep any result or ingredient claim accurate, and add text in your editor so it can be checked before posting.

faq.q: Is an AI creator video different from hiring a real UGC creator?
faq.a: Yes. You upload one photo and pay credits per clip instead of a creator rate, usage fees, and revision rounds. The person is AI-generated and not a real customer, so present the video as an ad rather than an independent review.
